summary: The Rise Above Movement, a Southern California white supremacist fight club founded around 2016, assaulted protesters at rallies including Charlottesville, then rebranded as a fascist MMA lifestyle clothing label run by co-founder Robert Rundo from Serbia.

evidence.note: group first appears after the 2016 election as DIY Division, renamed RAM in spring 2017
public debut brawl at a Huntington Beach MAGA rally in Southern California
overlap with Hammerskin neo-Nazi skinheads and their violent record
members attack counter-protesters at the Charlottesville torch march and main rally
FBI arrests, guilty pleas and prison terms; later charges dismissed on First Amendment grounds
European tour to neo-Nazi MMA events in Germany, France and a Kyiv nightclub
Rundo fights in Ukraine and meets the White Rex founder
Rundo's backstory: gang stabbing around age 18, radicalised in state prison
Bellingcat geolocates Rundo in Belgrade; he registers a company in Serbia
update: Serbia expels Rundo in February 2021 and his charges are reinstated in March

notes: Primary is the organization, so roles are empty; Rundo gets a long Part Two segment as a secondary subject. fascism-far-right chosen as primary because RAM mixes identitarian, Evola and Italian Fascist influences; nazism added as secondary for its open neo-Nazi symbolism. Covered span starts with Rundo's 2009 stabbing and prison radicalisation (approximate year); his juvenile arrest is mentioned briefly.
